input.quote: 13.1 Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13, shall continue in full force and effect, on a Product-by-Product and country-by-country basis until the Secondary Royalty Term with respect to such Product expires, at which time this Agreement shall expire in its entirety with respect to such Product in such country. Upon expiration of this Agreement, the licenses granted to Ono under Section 2.1 shall become non-exclusive, fully paid- up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights
input.rationale: There is no auto-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement: a document-wide search for "renew"/"automatically renew" returns only patent-term renewals and Section 14.4 (which expressly says post-expiry dealings are not a renewal or extension). Section 13.1 is expiry-based rather than renewal-based — the term runs on a Product-by-Product, country-by-country basis until the Secondary Royalty Term (defined in Section 1.55 as a finite period keyed off expiry of the Initial Royalty Term) expires, with no evergreen extension, no non-renewal notice window and no renewal price uplift. The structure also favours us: on expiry Ono's licences convert to perpetual, fully paid-up, royalty-free licences, and Section 13.2 gives Ono a unilateral without-cause termination right on notice. Because none of the risks the rule targets (long non-renewal notice windows, multi-year automatic renewals, uncapped uplifts) are present, the clause satisfies the preferred position by construction and no redline is warranted.
